header.running_head: The Signs of Dhikr and the Reality of Dhikr

blocks.text: narrates, "We were once with Rasulullaah ﷺ when we spoke of Jannah and Jahannam (with) so much (conviction) that it seemed to appear before our very eyes. I then went to my wife and children with whom I started laughing and playing. However, when I thought of the state of mind I had been in (with Rasulullaah ﷺ), I left the house. I then met Abu Bakr (RA), to whom I said, 'O Abu Bakr! I have become a Munaafiq.' 'Why do you say that?' he asked. I explained, 'When we are with Nabi ﷺ and he speaks to us about Jannah and Jahannam, it seems as if it is before our very eyes. However, when we leave his presence and become engrossed with our wives, children and occupations, we forget.' Abu Bakr (RA) remarked, 'But we do the same.' I then approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and mentioned this to him. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'O Handhala! If you can be with your families as you are when you are with me, the angels will actually shake hands with you on your beds and on the street. O Handhala! There are times for this and times for that.'" [^1]
Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "If you could remain at all times as you are when you are with me, the angels will even shade you with their wings." [^2]

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that he once said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! When we are with you, our hearts are softened, we detach ourselves from this world and yearn for the Aakhirah." Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "If after leaving me you remain as you are when with me, the angels will visit you and shake hands with you in the streets. On the other hand, if you do not sin, Allaah will create a creation that sins until their sins reach the heights of the sky. They will then seek forgiveness from Allaah and He will forgive them all their sins without any concern." [^3]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) would think of Allaah while Performing Tawaaf

Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) says, "We were performing Tawaaf when I extended to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) my proposal to marry his daughter, he remained silent and offered no reply. 'Had he been happy,' I said to myself, 'he would have certainly given me a reply. By Allaah! I shall never speak to him about it ever again.' It so happened that he reached Madinah before me and when I returned, I first went to the Masjid of Rasulullaah ﷺ where I greeted Rasulullaah ﷺ and fulfilled the rights owed to him. I then went to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA). He welcomed me most warmly and asked when I had arrived. When I informed him that I had just arrived, he said, 'Were you asking me about Sauda bint Abdullaah (my daughter) at a time when we were performing Tawaaf and could think of Allaah before our very eyes?
